q: Vasco da Gama's fleet arrived at Calicut in May 1498 and was received by which one of the following local rulers?
o: The Nawab of Bengal
The Raja of Cochin
The Zamorin (Samuthiri) of Calicut
The Sultan of Bijapur

q: Which one of the following statements about Alfonso de Albuquerque's tenure as Portuguese governor in India is correct?
o: He was the first Portuguese governor in India, preceding Francisco De Almeida
He acquired Goa from the Mughal emperor Akbar in 1530
He introduced the practice of sati in Portuguese territories for the first time
He acquired Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in 1510, making it the first Indian territory under European control since Alexander the Great, and abolished the practice of sati during his rule

q: Which one of the following was an important MILITARY contribution attributed to the Portuguese in India, later adopted by other European powers and eventually by Indian rulers such as the Marathas and Sikhs?
o: The construction of the first Indian naval dockyards under Chola patronage
A system of drilling groups of infantry on the Spanish model, introduced in the 1630s as a counter to Dutch pressure
The abolition of the mansabdari system
The introduction of gunpowder to India for the first time in recorded history

q: Which one of the following statements about the Dutch East India Company (VOC) and its activities in India is correct?
o: It never received powers to wage war, conclude treaties, or take possession of territory
It was formed in 1580 immediately following Francis Drake's circumnavigation voyage
It was formed in 1602 by the States-General of the Netherlands amalgamating several trading companies, and established its first Indian factory at Masulipatnam in 1605
Its first Indian factory was established at Surat, prior to any settlement in the Coromandel region

q: The 'Amboyna Massacre' of 1623, in which the Dutch killed ten Englishmen and nine Japanese at a location in present-day Indonesia, is significant for which one of the following reasons?
o: It led directly to the permanent expulsion of the Dutch from all of Asia
It marked the first ever confrontation between any two European powers in Asia
It resulted in an alliance between the Dutch and the Portuguese against the English
It intensified Anglo-Dutch rivalry in the East, eventually contributing to a 1667 compromise under which the English withdrew claims on Indonesia while the Dutch retired from India

q: With reference to Sir Thomas Roe's mission to the Mughal court (1615-1619), which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Though he failed to conclude a formal commercial treaty with Emperor Jahangir, he secured permission to set up English factories at Agra, Ahmedabad, and Broach
He successfully concluded a formal commercial treaty with Jahangir covering all of the Mughal empire
He represented the Dutch East India Company rather than the English
He was the first Englishman to ever visit the Mughal court, preceding Captain William Hawkins

q: Bombay came into the possession of the English East India Company through which one of the following routes?
o: It was granted by the Mughal emperor Farrukhsiyar as part of his 1717 farman

It was given to King Charles II of England as dowry upon his marriage to the Portuguese princess Catherine of Braganza in 1662, and later transferred to the Company in 1668 for an annual payment of ten pounds
It was seized militarily from the Dutch following the Battle of Hooghly
It was purchased directly by the East India Company from the Sultan of Bijapur in 1510

q: Which one of the following correctly describes the founding of the English settlement that became Calcutta?
o: Fort William was established in 1751, immediately following the Second Carnatic War

Job Charnock negotiated a treaty with the Mughals in February 1690 and returned to Sutanuti in August 1690; the Company later bought the zamindari of Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata in 1698, with the fortified settlement named Fort William in 1700
The English received Calcutta as part of the Golden Farman issued by the Sultan of Golconda in 1632
Calcutta was founded directly by Sir Thomas Roe during his 1615-1619 mission

q: The 1717 farman issued by the Mughal emperor Farrukhsiyar, popularly known as the 'Magna Carta of the (East India) Company', granted which one of the following privileges?
o: Exclusive rights over the Mughal empire's salt and opium trade

Exemption from additional customs duties in Bengal (beyond the earlier annual payment), permission to issue dastaks for goods transportation, and currency privileges for Company-minted Bombay coins across the Mughal empire
The permanent expulsion of the French and Dutch companies from Indian trade
Full sovereign control over the province of Bengal

q: The two rival English trading companies operating in India (following the 1688 English Revolution) were amalgamated in 1708 under which one of the following names?
o: The Governor and Company of Merchants of London
The Honourable East India Company
The Perpetual Company of the Indies
The United Company of Merchants of England Trading to the East Indies

q: Which one of the following statements about the French East India Company (Compagnie des Indes Orientales) is correct?
o: It was founded before the Portuguese, Dutch, and English companies, making the French the first Europeans to trade with India
It never established any settlements on India's east coast, operating exclusively on the west coast
Pondicherry was its first Indian settlement, founded immediately upon the company's establishment in 1664
It was founded in 1664 under the patronage of Louis XIV's minister Colbert, and was granted a 50-year monopoly on French trade in the Indian and Pacific Oceans

q: Which one of the following pairs of contenders was supported respectively by the French and the English during the Second Carnatic War (1749-54)?
o: French supported Nasir Jang and Anwar-ud-din Khan; English supported Muzaffar Jang and Chanda Sahib
French and English both remained neutral, leaving the succession disputes to be settled by the Marathas
French supported Muzaffar Jang (for the Deccan) and Chanda Sahib (for the Carnatic); English supported Nasir Jang and Anwar-ud-din Khan
Both France and England supported Muzaffar Jang and Chanda Sahib jointly

q: Robert Clive's celebrated defence of Arcot (1751) during the Second Carnatic War is best described by which one of the following?
o: Clive's Arcot campaign ended in a decisive French victory over the English

With only around 210 men, Clive captured Arcot as a diversionary tactic to relieve pressure on the besieged Trichinopoly, prompting Chanda Sahib to rush back with a much larger force but ultimately fail to retake the fort
Clive led a force of over 10,000 men to directly relieve the siege of Trichinopoly without any diversionary manoeuvre
Clive's action at Arcot took place during the Third Carnatic War, following the fall of Dupleix

q: Which one of the following statements about Joseph Francis Dupleix, the French governor in India, is correct?
o: He was conferred the title of 'Nawab' by the Mughal emperor and Muzaffar Jang, the subahdar of the Deccan, and is credited by historians with the qualities of an administrator, diplomat, and leader with broad political vision
He was the founder of Pondicherry as a French settlement in 1674
He led the Dutch forces during the Anglo-Dutch rivalry in India
He was the first French governor to establish a factory at Surat under Francois Caron in 1667

q: As French Governor-General of Pondicherry from 1741, Dupleix undertook which one of the following administrative measures, despite facing several challenges including Maratha invasion and famine?
o: He dismantled Pondicherry's role as a commercial emporium in favour of purely military functions
He abandoned Pondicherry entirely in favour of relocating French headquarters to Chandernagore

He reduced public expenditure and balanced income and expenditure (including cutting officers' salaries), while disobeying Company directors by enhancing Pondicherry's fortifications using his own personal wealth
He fully complied with all Company directives, including reducing Pondicherry's fortifications to save costs
